subject: Bilal Ahmad
description: Verified public-profile knowledge used by Ask Mintorian. Records are authored from the Mintorian website and the public CV included in this repository.

records.title: Professional and research profile
records.summary: Bilal Ahmad is a PhD student at the University of Bath whose work combines power-system reliability, battery energy storage systems and machine-learning-enabled decision support. Alongside his research, he holds two part-time Full Stack Developer roles and previously served as a Technical Lead in machine learning at HCL Technologies.
details: His research combines data-driven learning with physically interpretable models.
The stated goals include grid resilience, flexibility and transparent decision support.
His profile spans academic research, electrical engineering, applied machine learning and software engineering.
His two current part-time, remote Full Stack Developer roles are at Dystil.AI and Just Jutz; both are listed from April 2026 to present.

records.title: Core research focus
records.summary: Bilal researches power-system reliability, battery energy storage systems (BESS), optimal power flow and security-constrained optimal power flow (OPF/SCOPF), and explainable AI for intelligent contingency screening.
details: The work focuses on energy-system operations and planning.
It uses machine learning alongside physically interpretable power-system models.
Distribution-network resilience, uncertainty and adverse-weather preparedness are recurring themes.

records.title: PhD in Power System Reliability
records.summary: Bilal is pursuing a PhD at the University of Bath on power-system reliability.
details: The public CV describes research on power-distribution-network preparedness for severe weather events involving compound hazards.
The work includes an automated optimal-procurement strategy framework for Distribution Network Operators (DNOs).
The work applies explainable AI to intelligent contingency screening for power-system reliability.
